discovery: Spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots: proposal and experimental realization of coherent control and readout of single electron spins

nominees.name: Seigo Tarucha
nominees.affiliation: RIKEN Center for Quantum Computing, Japan

nominees.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
nominees.affiliation: QuTech and Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

subfield: Condensed matter physics / mesoscopic physics and quantum devices
motivation: Loss (with DiVincenzo) proposed in 1998 that the spin of a single electron confined in a gate-defined semiconductor quantum dot could serve as a qubit, with exchange-based two-qubit gates. Tarucha established the few-electron quantum dot as an artificial atom with controllable shell filling and later pioneered micromagnet-based electric spin control and high-fidelity gates. Vandersypen achieved single-shot spin readout and coherent single-spin rotations, and then programmable multi-qubit processors in silicon. Together they turned Coulomb blockade and spin physics in nanostructures into a controllable quantum technology, now pursued industrially on CMOS-compatible platforms. The theory was validated step by step by experiments that confronted charge noise, nuclear spins and valley physics head-on. This is mesoscopic physics at its best: a quantum-mechanical subtlety made into a scalable, engineered device.
